claims.text: A controlled pre-exposure oxidation treatment can form a uniform, stable, passivating oxide film on Q235 steel.
The protective surface film on Q235 steel consists primarily of Fe2O3 and Fe3O4.
The pre-formed iron oxide layer is stable under the proposed corrosive exposure conditions.
An intact oxide layer limits the ingress of chloride ions and water to the underlying Q235 steel.
Limiting the ingress of chloride ions and water suppresses corrosion of the underlying steel.
Mechanical or chemical disruption of the oxide film removes its barrier function.
Loss of the oxide barrier accelerates corrosion-related degradation.
Elevated temperature and aggressive chemical environments enhance corrosion after disruption of the oxide barrier.
Q235 specimens with an intact pre-formed oxide layer will have lower corrosion rates than untreated Q235 specimens.
Q235 specimens with an intact pre-formed oxide layer will exhibit less surface degradation than untreated specimens.
Q235 specimens with deliberately disrupted oxide films will have higher corrosion rates than untreated specimens.
Untreated Q235 steel develops naturally evolving, non-uniform oxide films.
The proposed protective effect applies in controlled chloride-containing environments from approximately 25°C to 80°C.
Additional mechanical stress or alloying variations may alter the proposed protective effect.
